headline: The Kreditanstalt takes over the Volksbank
text: On 6 January the Kreditanstalt announced it is taking over the Schweizerische Volksbank for 2.6 billion francs. The Volksbank, the fourth-largest Swiss bank, has been weakened by write-downs on property loans and had to raise its reserves to 500 million francs last year. The Bankgesellschaft, which also bid, lost out at the last moment. Chairman Rainer Gut and the new chief executive Josef Ackermann expect large savings from 1995.
imageCaption: Robert A. Jecker, general manager of the Schweizerische Kreditanstalt, 1991

headline: Record loss, dividend slashed, Akers out
text: IBM lost 4.97 billion dollars in 1992, including a fourth-quarter loss of 5.46 billion, the largest in its history. On 26 January the board cut the quarterly dividend from 1.21 dollars to 54 cents and announced that chairman John Akers will step down. Standard & Poor's downgraded IBM's debt.
imageCaption: John Akers, IBM's chairman and chief executive

headline: Earnings up 20% in 1992, but the stock only kept pace
text: Coca-Cola's earnings per share and operating income rose 20% in 1992 (excluding accounting changes), after 19% in 1991, and its share of world soft drink sales reached a record 43%. Volume growth slowed to 3% as recessions hit markets such as Brazil. The share price rose only 4.4%, in line with the market, for a total return of 5.8% after 75% in 1991; the company says it is 'downright unhappy'. The board raised the quarterly dividend 21%.
imageCaption: Roberto Goizueta, chief executive of Coca-Cola
imageCredit: rights holder not named on the source page

headline: Berkshire's book value up 20% in 1992; Buffett back from Salomon
text: Buffett's letter of 1 March reports that book value per share rose 20.3% in 1992, to 7,745 dollars, a compound 23.6% a year over 28 years. Last June Buffett stepped down as interim chairman of Salomon Inc after ten months; Salomon Brothers has since reported record pre-tax earnings.
imageCaption: One New York Plaza, long the head office of Salomon Brothers

headline: McDonald's: 111 record quarters in a row
text: McDonald's reported that 1992 was its 111th consecutive quarter of record systemwide sales, net income and earnings per share. Net income rose to 959 million dollars on systemwide sales of 21.9 billion. It had about 13,100 restaurants in 65 countries, more than 4,100 of them outside the United States.
source: https://archive.org/download/mcdonaldscorpannualreports/mcdonalds1992_djvu.txt (1992 annual report, read 2026-10-03); https://archive.org/download/mcdonaldscorpannualreports/mcdonalds1994_djvu.txt (1994 annual report, 11-year summary, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Big Mac

headline: 'Marlboro Friday': Philip Morris cuts the price of Marlboro
text: On Friday 2 April Philip Morris announced a 20% price cut for Marlboro to win back smokers who are switching to cheap generic cigarettes. Its shares fell 26% that day, and other brand-name consumer companies such as Coca-Cola and RJR Nabisco fell too. Investors fear that brands no longer allow premium prices.
imageCaption: Marlboro packs on a production line
imageCredit: Will Mcintyre/The LIFE Images Collection/Getty Images

headline: Enron's giant power station in England starts up
text: Enron's Teesside power station near Middlesbrough in north-east England has been commissioned after 29 months of construction. With 1,875 megawatts it is the largest gas-fired combined-cycle plant in Europe and can supply almost 3% of the electricity of England, Wales and Scotland.
imageCaption: Teesside Power Station near Middlesbrough

headline: Cisco's profit doubles again
text: On May 6 Cisco reported sales of $172 million for the quarter to April 25, up 89% from a year earlier, and net income of $46 million, up 99%. For the first nine months of its fiscal year sales are up 94% to $444 million.
imageCaption: Groundbreaking for Cisco's San Jose campus, 1993
imageCredit: Cisco Systems (Center for Cisco Heritage archive, Computer History Museum)

headline: Bernd Pischetsrieder takes over from von Kuenheim
text: Eberhard von Kuenheim handed over the chairmanship of BMW on 13 May after 23 years and moves to the supervisory board. In his time the company grew from 20,000 to 70,000 employees and to sales of 30 billion marks. His successor is Bernd Pischetsrieder rather than the development chief Wolfgang Reitzle.
imageCaption: Bernd Pischetsrieder, who became BMW chairman in 1993

headline: Jurassic Park breaks the box-office record
text: Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park opened in American cinemas on 11 June and took 50.1 million dollars in its first weekend, a new record. Its dinosaurs were made with computer-generated images by Industrial Light & Magic and with life-sized animatronic models.
imageCaption: Poster for Jurassic Park, 1993

headline: Apple replaces its chief executive as a price war eats its profit
text: On 18 June Apple's board replaced John Sculley as chief executive with Michael Spindler, until now the number two; Sculley stays on as chairman. A price war among PC makers is forcing Apple to sell its Macintosh computers ever more cheaply, and its profit is shrinking fast. The shares lost 30% in June.
imageCaption: John Sculley, 2014

headline: Banks expected to report 'brilliant results'
text: Swiss shares stayed in demand in July: the franc is strong and attractive as a safe haven after new tension in the European currency system, and falling interest rates push money into dividend shares. Analysts at the Zürcher Kantonalbank see room for another 20% rise and expect the banks to contribute with excellent results, and lower loan provisions from next year. Bankverein bearer shares gained 5.3% in the last week of July and are up 58% since the end of 1992.
source: Neue Zürcher Zeitung, 31 July 1993, p. 29 ('Die Zürcher Börse vom 26. bis zum 30. Juli: Anhaltende Attraktivität des Schweizer Marktes'), scan data/manual/scans/nzz/NZZ_1993-07-31.pdf (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Bankverein building at Aeschenplatz in Basel, long the home of the Schweizerischer Bankverein

headline: Gerstner takes an 8.9 billion dollar charge and cuts 35,000 jobs
text: IBM reported a second-quarter loss of 8.04 billion dollars after an 8.9 billion dollar restructuring charge, and will cut 35,000 more jobs, shrinking to about 225,000 employees by the end of 1994. The dividend was cut again, to 25 cents a quarter. 'The No. 1 priority is to restore the company to profitability,' Gerstner said.
imageCaption: Louis Gerstner, IBM's new chairman and chief executive, in his 1993 executive portrait
imageCredit: IBM (executive biography files, 1993; no photographer named on the page)

headline: Mosaic: a program that makes the internet something to look at
text: Two programmers at the University of Illinois, Marc Andreessen and Eric Bina, have written Mosaic, a 'browser' for the World Wide Web, and since September it also runs on ordinary Windows and Macintosh computers. It is the first that shows pictures and text together on one page, and to move from page to page a click of the mouse is enough. It is free and easy to install. There is not much to see so far: late last year the whole Web consisted of 26 sites.
imageCaption: File:NCSAMosaic1.0Mac.png

headline: Sculley leaves Apple for good; Spindler cuts jobs
text: John Sculley, replaced as chief executive in June, has now left Apple altogether after a bad year and a price war in personal computers; Michael Spindler runs the company and is cutting jobs, projects and research. Under Sculley sales grew from about 800 million to 7.9 billion dollars a year.
imageCaption: The Apple Newton MessagePad, launched August 1993

headline: Sony announces it will enter the games console market
text: On 27 October Sony said it is entering the video game console market with a machine called PlayStation, built around 3D graphics. Sony and its Japanese music company have set up Sony Computer Entertainment, led by engineer Ken Kutaragi, to run the business.
imageCaption: Ken Kutaragi, who led Sony's PlayStation project

headline: Brent sinks toward $14
text: North Sea Brent fell to about $14 a barrel by the end of November and US crude to about $15, the lowest in five years, as OPEC members overproduce and demand is weak.
imageCaption: The Brent A and Brent B oil platforms in the North Sea

headline: Boeing launches the 737 Next Generation
text: On 17 November Boeing announced the 737 Next Generation, an updated family of its best-selling small jet, with new wings and engines, to compete with the Airbus A320.
imageCaption: A Boeing 737-800, a member of the Next Generation family, takes off

headline: 1993 in review: low interest rates, modest gains
text: The S&P 500 gained 7% in 1993 to 466.45. The Dow closed above 3,500 for the first time on 19 May and ended the year at 3,754.09, up 13.7%. The yield on 30-year Treasury bonds has fallen to about 6.2 percent, which helps shares and borrowers.
imageCaption: Traders in the corn pit of the Chicago Board of Trade, 1993
imageCredit: Jeremy Kemp (moved from en:Image:Chicago bot.jpg on the English Wikipedia). en:Image:Chicago bot.jpg

headline: No recovery in sight for Japan's banks
text: Most of 1993 passed without a clear sign of economic recovery. The troubles of the housing loan companies, the jusen, which borrowed heavily from banks, first hit the headlines this year.
imageCaption: Shibuya crossing in Tokyo at night, October 1992

headline: LDDS merges with Metromedia's and Resurgens' phone businesses
text: LDDS has combined with Metromedia Communications and Resurgens Communications Group, making it a national long-distance carrier with Bernard Ebbers as chief executive. Billionaire John Kluge, owner of Metromedia, becomes a major shareholder. Sales are on course for about $1.1 billion this year.
imageCaption: Telephone exchange, 1975
